steps.title: Create a Connected App, or External Client App
steps.detail: In Setup, create a Connected App, or an External Client App, which Salesforce recommends starting in Spring 26. Give it a unique name. The API name is used for the developer name.
steps.blockerTip: Check the current Setup menu in your org. Connected Apps and External Client Apps are different models, do not mix their settings.

steps.title: Enable OAuth and set the callback URL
steps.detail: Enable OAuth Settings and enter your exact Callback URL. Add Selected OAuth Scopes, minimum only, for example api for API access, and refresh_token and offline_access if you need refresh tokens.
steps.blockerTip: The callback URL must match your code exactly. A placeholder callback will fail in a real flow.

steps.title: Get the Consumer Key and Secret
steps.detail: Save the app, then go to Manage Consumer Details and copy the Consumer Key and Consumer Secret. Store the secret server side.
steps.blockerTip: Never put the Consumer Secret in client code or a public repo.

steps.title: Test OAuth in a sandbox or dev org
steps.detail: Test the authorization code flow in a sandbox or dev org first, with one API call. Set refresh token policy to valid until revoked if you need long lived refresh tokens.
steps.blockerTip: Test in production only after sandbox works. A production callback or scope change can break an install.

steps.title: List publicly only if you need to
steps.detail: For AppExchange listing, complete the security review separately. Do not promise a listing date until that review is done.
steps.blockerTip: Security review is separate from app creation. Creating the app does not mean it is listed.
